source: Voudouris, Crosby, Beyret, Hernandez-Orallo, Shanahan, Halina, Cheke (2022) Direct Human-AI Comparison in the Animal-AI Environment
finding: First direct child vs AI comparison on animal-cognition tests (Animal-AI testbed, includes trap-tube and string-pulling tasks). Children beat 30 AI agents overall. On causal level 10 both children and agents did poorly.
numbers: n=52 children aged 6-10 vs 30 AIs, 40 tasks. Children mean 0.605 (median 0.628, SD 0.148); AIs mean 0.341 (median 0.353, SD 0.081). 0% of AIs passed on average levels 3, 6, 8, 9, 10. Level 10: agents matched the average child on string-pulling, were worse on block-pushing tool tasks.
limits: AIs are 2019 competition RL agents, not LLMs. Embodiment and reaction-time confounds. Children's score fell with level number, AI score did not.
agent_relevance: Old RL agents pass many 'causal' tasks by cue learning, not by understanding. Same warning as the crow work: need a transfer test the agent was not fitted to (G3).

source: Voudouris et al. (2022) same paper: control for rational behaviour
finding: The paper notes that trap controls (a non-functional trap on top of the tube) are sometimes failed even by adult humans who know things do not fall up (Silva et al. 2005).
numbers: No new numbers; citation to Silva, Page, Silva 2005 as a boundary condition of trap-avoidance control.
limits: Second-hand report of Silva 2005; the primary paper was not opened.
agent_relevance: A pass on the harder transfer variant can still hide failure on the control; test controls on the agent as well as the transfer item.

source: Crosby/Voudouris et al. (2024) The Animal-AI Environment: a virtual laboratory for comparative cognition and AI research (Animal-AI 3)
finding: Animal-AI 3 testbed has 900 tasks over 10 levels, includes a trap-tube task and string-pulling. Dreamer-v3, PPO and a heuristic agent tested against children. Causal reasoning, object permanence and numerosity levels were hard for all agents including children.
numbers: Odds of passing vs random agent: children 47x, ironbar and Trrrrr 19x, Dreamer-v3 6.5x (p=0.038), PPO not above chance (p=0.61). Causal Reasoning level odds 0.367 vs Food Retrieval (p<1e-6). Dreamer-v3 would have placed 25th of 64 in the 2019 competition.
limits: Model-based RL with curriculum; no LLM. Authors leave better curricula to future work.
agent_relevance: Ready-made public place to run a trap-tube-like transfer item for an LLM agent loop, with chance and child baselines.

source: Mecattaf, Slater, Tesic, Prunty, Voudouris, Cheke (2024) A little less conversation, a little more action, please: physical common-sense of LLMs in a 3D embodied environment
finding: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro controlled an agent in Animal-AI via a ReAct prompt on 40 testbed tasks (4 per level). Children did better at every level. LLMs never exceeded the top-10 competition RL agents.
numbers: 40 tasks, 3 runs per task at temperature 0; children n=59 aged 6-10. Level 10 (causal): LLMs about equal to competition agents but at very low success; child error bars overlap LLM scores only at levels 4, 5, 9, 10 where LLM scores are near floor.
limits: Coarse action-script control and one 512x512 image per turn may dominate the result; authors say so. Floor effects hide differences at hard levels.
agent_relevance: First published LLM test on the same paradigm family as the crow trap-tube; a text-and-image agent fails when it must act, not just answer.

source: Mecattaf et al. (2024) Experiment 2: in-context expert example
finding: Adding one worked example of a tutorial level (in-context learning) gave no notable improvement. Effects went in different directions per model.
numbers: Claude: slightly worse L1, better L2, L3 same. Gemini: no effect on L1, lower on L2 and L3. GPT-4o: L1 same, L2 and L3 higher; its L3 matched the upper range of competition agents and the lower range of children.
limits: No numbers beyond figure bars; small subset of tasks.
agent_relevance: A single demonstration is not a reliable scaffold for physical-causal tasks; it can hurt. Do not assume few-shot transfers (G3).

source: Voudouris, Cheke, Schulz (2025) Bringing comparative cognition to computers
finding: Argues AI testing should copy comparative-cognition rules: avoid under-attribution (dogs failed invisible displacement because of the container, not memory; LLM arithmetic fails from tokenization) and over-attribution (Clever Hans; image nets use texture).
numbers: No new data. Examples: dog object permanence; large-number sums fail from tokenization; adversarial examples collapse accuracy.
quote: AI research has its own Clever Hans moments
limits: Position paper, 3 pages.
agent_relevance: Supports building the schema's transfer checks as control conditions: each pass needs a Clever-Hans control and each fail a task-validity check.

source: Yiu, Kosoy, Gopnik (2023/2024) Transmission versus truth, imitation versus innovation: what children can do that LLMs cannot (yet)
finding: Tool-choice task: when the usual tool is missing, pick the functional but unrelated object (plant pot) over the associated but useless one (coffee lid). Children and adults mostly innovate. Text models mostly pick the associate.
numbers: Children 3-7 y (n=42): association 88.4% (SE 2.8), innovation 85.2% (SE 3.2). Adults (n=30): association 84.9%, innovation 95.7% (SE 1.0). Models: gpt-3.5-turbo, text-davinci-003, Claude, FLAN-T5 XXL, Bloomz were near human on association, much worse on innovation.
limits: 2023 models, text only, exact LLM percentages not given in the perspective. Authors say the models sometimes cited their own published blicket papers (contamination).
agent_relevance: The LLM analogue of cue vs cause: nearest-neighbour association wins unless the function is made explicit. A step that restates the goal in functional terms before choosing a tool is worth testing.

source: Yiu, Kosoy, Gopnik (2024) same: blicket data given as text
finding: Models given the children's blicket evidence as text struggled to extract causal over-hypotheses (is the rule OR or AND?). Deep RL and behaviour cloning also failed. Children learned from a handful of observations including their own interventions.
numbers: No per-model figures reported in this perspective.
limits: Summary-level claim; details live in Kosoy et al. 2022 and later work.
agent_relevance: Evidence should carry the agent's own interventions; reading someone else's log is weaker (see c17).

source: Kosoy, Reagan, Lai, Gopnik, Cobb (2023) Comparing machines and children: developmental psychology experiments with LaMDA
finding: LaMDA scored lowest on the causal-reasoning domain of a battery of classic child experiments. It copied the common causal pattern and failed on unusual ones.
numbers: LaMDA Response Score (LRS): causal domain 1.34; perception 2.91; theory of mind 2.86; social-moral 4.33. Gear task: simple A-pushes-B 3.42, conjunctive A+B 2.02. Blicket induction 0.98 and 1.06. Disjunctive/conjunctive blicket 0.44 to 1.12.
limits: Single model (LaMDA), 2023, rubric scored by two blind coders. Model sometimes quoted blicket papers; authors renamed blickets 'zerpdas'.
agent_relevance: Renaming novel terms to defeat contamination is a cheap control to copy for any transfer item (G3).

source: Kosoy, Chan, Liu, Collins, Gopnik et al. (2022) Towards understanding how machines can learn causal overhypotheses
finding: Blicket environment with disjunctive vs conjunctive rules. GPT-3 (text-davinci-002) and PaLM tested on text descriptions. Few-shot with a covering overhypothesis set helps PaLM; adding reasoning to the prompt did not help.
numbers: Small hand-scored table: e.g. given hypotheses, disjunctive, GPT-3 freeform 1/1 correct but 6 wrong extra blickets; PaLM never named objects from the other machine. PaLM two-shot fails when the test overhypothesis is not covered by the shots.
limits: Tiny n per cell; temperature 0.7 for GPT-3, 0 for PaLM; no statistics.
agent_relevance: Few-shot works only inside the shown hypothesis space. A schema that must discover a new rule type should not lean on few-shot examples.

source: Jin et al. (2023/24) Can large language models infer causation from correlation? (Corr2Cause)
finding: 17 LLMs on pure causal inference from correlation statements: near random. Fine-tuned models score high on the original set but collapse on paraphrased or renamed variants.
numbers: Best F1 33.38 (BART MNLI); GPT-3 Instruct (text-davinci-003) F1 29.08 with precision 20.92 and recall 47.66. Several models below random. Fine-tuned models drop to as low as 39.29 on the paraphrased set and up to 62.30 after variable refactorization.
limits: Table lists 29.08 for text-davinci-003; a 2025 paper cites it as GPT-4. Check before quoting. Formal-logic task, not physical.
agent_relevance: A pass on training-format items is not evidence of causal inference; a perturbation test is the right check (G3).

source: Sun, Nogueira, Silva (2025) Structured thinking matters: improving LLM generalization in causal inference tasks
finding: Having a reasoning model first build a knowledge graph of the correlation premises, then answer, raised Corr2Cause F1.
numbers: Qwen3-32B F1 32.71 to 48.26 (+47.5% relative). Random-uniform F1 reported as 20.38.
limits: Single model, test subset only, no perturbation test reported in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Evidence that an explicit intermediate structure beats direct answering on a causal task; fits the idea of code holding state.

source: Kiciman, Ness, Sharma, Tan (2023/24) Causal reasoning and large language models: opening a new frontier for causality
finding: GPT-3.5/4 beat existing algorithms at pairwise causal direction, counterfactuals and necessary/sufficient cause from text. Success rides on variable names and world knowledge, not on data.
numbers: Tubingen pairs: GPT-4 97% vs prior best 83%; counterfactual 92% (+20); actual causality 86%. Old models (ada to text-davinci-002) about 0.50. New post-cutoff pair set (67 pairs): GPT-3.5 80.3%, GPT-4 98.5%.
limits: Authors warn of unpredictable failures; the tasks are knowledge retrieval, not discovery. The 67-pair set is small.
agent_relevance: LLMs can look causal on vignettes by retrieval. Do not read this as the ability to discover a new mechanism; pair with intervention tests.

source: Lampinen, Chan, Dasgupta, Nam, Wang (2023) Passive learning of active causal strategies in agents and language models
finding: Agents trained on passive expert data can learn to intervene, if they predict natural-language explanations; explanations also de-confound training data. Chinchilla 70B learned an odd-one-out intervention strategy from four few-shot examples that included explanations and reasoning.
numbers: LM test: 4 shots, relevant dimension drawn from two of three (colour, shape, texture), tested on the held-out third. 5 seeds per RL condition. Figures give success rates; exact values not read from text.
limits: Synthetic environment; no animal task. Held-out dimension transfer is positive evidence here, unlike GPT-3 in c10.
agent_relevance: Strongest published sign that explanation text in the prompt can carry a causal strategy across a held-out dimension. Good model for an S4 transfer probe.

source: GX-Chen, Lin, Samiei, Precup, Richards, Fergus, Marino (2025) Language agents mirror human causal reasoning biases (COLM 2025)
finding: In the blicket test, LM agents infer OR rules but fail on equally evidenced AND rules (disjunctive bias) across model families, sizes and prompting. The bias looks like adults, not 4-year-olds.
numbers: Models: gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner, qwq, gemma3:27b. Prompts: default, CoT, ReAct, Reflexion. Info-gain oracle gets Q&A accuracy 1.0. All models drop going from 4 to 8 objects and from OR to AND. LMs explore less in OR worlds, children do not.
limits: Exact accuracies only in figures. Human data reused from Gopnik et al. 2017.
agent_relevance: Prompt style (CoT, ReAct, Reflexion) did not remove the bias: it is a prior problem, not a depth problem. Supports not adding reflection steps (G1).

source: GX-Chen et al. (2025) same: test-time hypothesis sampling
finding: Fix: sample many distinct hypotheses as code from the LM, reject duplicates to flatten the prior, then pick the action that eliminates most hypotheses. With enough samples the AND vs OR gap disappears and exploration is no longer biased.
numbers: Initial unique hypotheses 16 to 96 in the 8-object world; more samples gave better exploration and Q&A with no conjunctive deficit.
limits: Needs a small closed hypothesis space coded as functions; cost grows with samples.
agent_relevance: Concrete scaffold the schema could use: code-held hypothesis set plus elimination, selected by code (G5), not by model judgement.

source: Samiei, Yiu, GX-Chen, Lin, Shen, Richards, Gopnik, Precup (2026) Human adults and LLMs as scientists: who benefits from active exploration? (CogSci 2026)
finding: Nexiom-detector (blicket-style) task. Adults with free interventions do well on AND rules, so the old conjunctive handicap came from passive evidence. Six LLMs given the same action space: some match adults on accuracy, but explore less efficiently and keep an AND gap.
numbers: Adults: 102 active, 102 passive observers, 102 passive proposers. Conjunctive object identification: proposers 0.12, observers 0.45, active 0.69; rule selection 0.57, 0.69, 0.82. 288 LLM trials over gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, gemini-2.5-flash, deepseek-reasoner, o4-mini, deepseek-chat. gpt-5 and deepseek-reasoner near-perfect on OR; deepseek-chat and o4-mini only modestly above random on AND.
limits: Conference paper, exact LLM numbers in figures only. Human test counts per figure text: about 9.6 (AND) vs 6.4 (OR).
agent_relevance: Active interventions matter only when tied to the agent's own outcomes (proposers did worst). Let the loop see the results of its own tests.

source: Alderete, Benthall, Xu, Xing (2026) Separable pathways for causal reasoning: architectural scaffolding for hypothesis-space restructuring in LLM agents
finding: Blicket variants where the rule silently changes mid-run. A context graph (typed state machine) lifts reasoning quality; dynamic behaviours (monitors that fire on contradicting evidence) lift whether reasoning happens at all. Run on Claude Sonnet 4.5, with Haiku 4.5 as trigger judge.
numbers: 1,085 trials. Run 08 (n=50 per arm): reasoning-eligible accuracy Base 73.3% (22/30), CG 93.9% (31/33; +20.6pp, p=0.038, h=0.59), CG+DB 95.3% (41/43). Exactly-N failure CG 28% (14/50) vs CG+DB 6% (3/50), p=0.003. Combined easy-rule n=110: raw Base 87.3%, CG 77.3%, CG+DB 89.1%. Trigger sensitivity 100% over 136 firings.
limits: Vendor authors, single model family, preprint; the scaffold made raw accuracy worse without the monitor, and some raw gains were not significant.
agent_relevance: Direct match to the schema: a code monitor that fires only on a contradicting output (G1, G2) plus a state machine. Warns that structure alone can hurt unless the revision trigger is present.

source: Piriyakulkij, Langenfeld, Le, Ellis (2024) Doing experiments and revising rules with natural language and probabilistic reasoning (NeurIPS 2024)
finding: LLM proposes natural-language rule hypotheses, code runs them, Monte Carlo updates beliefs, and experiments are chosen by expected information gain. Matches human Zendo data better than an LLM playing the game directly with ReAct.
numbers: Model explains 57% of variation in fine-grained human accuracy; a weaker fit of R2 = .05 is also reported; direct ReAct play only loosely correlated with humans. Removing explicit hypotheses, fuzzy rules or online updates broke the human fit.
limits: Zendo and ACRE tasks, GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-3.5; not animal paradigms. Read selectively.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as c16: model proposes, code scores and selects. Fuzzy rules matter, so do not discard a hypothesis on one noisy test.

source: Jin et al. (2023) CLadder: assessing causal reasoning in language models
finding: 10K questions across Pearl's rungs (association, intervention, counterfactual) with commonsense, anti-commonsense and nonsense stories to separate memory from reasoning. A causal chain-of-thought (CausalCoT) helped GPT-4.
numbers: CausalCoT 70.40% vs vanilla GPT-4 about 62.03% (+8.37 points). GPT-3 variants, LLaMa and Alpaca near random.
limits: Read abstract, intro and dataset description; per-rung values not verified. Text vignettes.
agent_relevance: Anti-commonsense and nonsense variants are the LLM version of removing arbitrary cues, as Taylor et al. did for the crows.

source: Bugaud (2026) CheeseBench: evaluating LLMs on rodent behavioural neuroscience paradigms
finding: Nine rodent paradigms as ASCII gridworlds with scalar reward only; 13 LLMs. Frontier models reach rodent level. Chain-of-thought and longer history hurt.
numbers: Random 38.0%; rodent reference about 78.9%; best open-weight (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) 68.0%; Claude Opus 4.7 86.7%. Prompt: default 46.7% vs CoT 31.9%, minimal 35.6%, few-shot 29.6%. History h=1 57.0% vs h=10 26.7%. Same model 20% to 57% by interface alone. 15 trials per cell (95% CI about +-25pp).
limits: No causal tool task in the nine paradigms; rodent baselines approximate. Noisy ablations.
agent_relevance: Interface and prompt choices moved scores more than model size: pin the harness before comparing scaffolds. CoT hurting in exploration tasks echoes G1.

source: Tang et al. (2026) CausalPhys: benchmark for causally-informed physical reasoning in VLMs
finding: 3,062 video and image questions in four domains (Perception, Anticipation, Intervention, Goal Orientation) with expert causal graphs; VLMs often give plausible but wrong answers, weak on relations. Causal-rationale fine-tuning helped.
numbers: N=3,062; an overall accuracy of 58.9% (95% CI 57.2 to 60.6) in an appendix bootstrap; fine-tuning with causal rationales raised Qwen2-VL-7B on PhysBench 58.3 to 62.3 (+4.0).
limits: Which model gives 58.9% not checked. Vision-language, not a tool task. Needs training, so not usable by a scaffold-only agent.
agent_relevance: Relation errors dominate physical-causal failures; a checklist of entity-relation facts before acting is a cheap scaffold idea.

source: Taylor, Hunt, Medina, Gray (2009) Do New Caledonian crows solve physical problems through causal reasoning? Proc R Soc B 276:247
finding: Search snippets only (page blocked by a browser check): crows that solved the trap-tube kept avoiding the trap when arbitrary cues were removed, but did not avoid it when a hole and a functional trap were present.
numbers: Snippet: 3 of 6 crows solved the initial trap-tube; no further numbers verified.
limits: Not opened; numbers belong to the angle A and B agents.
agent_relevance: The target design for an LLM analogue: train on cue-rich items, test on cue-free and structurally different items, include a control where the cue misleads.

source: Schaffer et al. (2024) ungulate cognition including trap-tube task, Sci Rep
finding: Search listing only: trap tube used as a measure of causal understanding in ungulates.
numbers: No numbers verified.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Shows the paradigm is still in use in 2024 outside corvids.

source: Search negative result (2026-10-31)
finding: No paper found that gives an LLM the crow trap-tube, trap-table or Aesop's fable task directly. Closest are Animal-AI trap-tube items, blicket tests, Corr2Cause, CLadder and CheeseBench.
numbers: Searches run: LLM + trap tube, LLM + Aesop, Animal-AI causal, tool innovation LLM. The arXiv API returned empty responses.
limits: Absence from a few searches, not proof.
agent_relevance: Gap to fill: an in-house text trap-tube with relabelled cues would be novel and a clean S4 transfer probe.
